E1.evidence: Public issue ros-industrial/motoman#122 (gavanderhoorn, maintainer, 2016-08-24): "It would seem `link_t` in the MH5 xacro macro is currently not at the correct position:" with an rviz screenshot, and "It looks like this is a [transform issue](.../motoman_mh5_support/urdf/mh5_macro.xacro#L164), and not related to the origin of the mesh." Fixed by PR #173 (geoffreychiou, merged 2017-05-23: '-			<origin xyz="0.0510 0 0" rpy="0 0 0"/>' -> '+			<origin xyz="0.0865 0 0" rpy="0 0 0"/>' for joint_t in mh5_macro.xacro, "Modified the x location of joint_t's origin to match the value from the data sheet.") and PR #175 (merge commit 1ec8ca1b, 2017-06-05, the same change in the generated motoman_mh5_support/urdf/mh5.urdf plus base_link visual/collision origins and joint_l limits); maintainer comments "This should be fixed with the merge of #173." and "Actually it was only half fixed...now fully fixed in #175".

E2.evidence: The candidate composition is the MH5 robot description (package motoman_mh5_support: urdf/mh5_macro.xacro, urdf/mh5.urdf and the meshes they reference) and its consumers (rviz's RobotModel display and robot_state_publisher, which computed the TF frames overlaid in the screenshot). The defect is a wrong constant inside the description itself: the origin of joint_t (link_b -> link_t) was 0.0510 m instead of the data-sheet value 0.0865 m, so the link_t mesh and TF frame are placed 35.5 mm from where the MH5 geometry puts them. Every correct consumer renders exactly what the description states; the failure does not depend on any assumption between the description and rviz or robot_state_publisher and would occur with any correct peer. The disagreement is between the description and the physical robot's geometry (the data sheet), which is not a unit with a declared interface in this source. The resolving edits (PR #173, #175) are confined to the support package. Step 2 stops the walk: internal.

E3.evidence: Not reached (ineligible at E2). Had it been eligible the operation would be PAIR (robot description feeding rviz / robot_state_publisher).

E4.evidence: Not reached. The observed effect in the source is visual only (rviz screenshot of link_t at the wrong position); no message, warning or motion is documented.

ineligible_reason: E2 step 2 (internal): the wrong joint_t origin is a constant inside the motoman_mh5_support robot description; consumers (rviz, robot_state_publisher) render it faithfully, so the failure does not depend on any assumption between two units and the fix only edits the description (xacro macro in #173, generated URDF in #175).
notes: The listed fix commit 1ec8ca1b is the merge of PR #175 (base kinetic-devel), which regenerates mh5.urdf after PR #173 (merge 65e8869f) changed mh5_macro.xacro; it also changes joint_l limits ('lower="-1.0122" upper="3.2218"', with the comment that the old data-sheet limits 'were clearly way off') and adds 'rpy="0 0 3.14159"' origins to the base_link visual and collision meshes; none of these involve a second unit. The mh5.urdf file header says 'EDITING THIS FILE BY HAND IS NOT RECOMMENDED': the xacro macro is the source, the URDF a generated copy, and their disagreement between #173 and #175 (2017-05-23 to 2017-06-05) is an inconsistency inside the same package. A real MH5 controller and its MotoROS driver would expose the wrong flange position as a wrong Cartesian pose only through this description; that composition is not documented in the source.
